title: The Lost Boarding Pass
statement: $100$ passengers board a plane with $100$ assigned seats, in order. The first passenger lost their pass and sits in a uniformly random seat. Every later passenger sits in their own seat if it is free, and otherwise in a uniformly random free seat. What is the probability that the last passenger gets their own seat?
insight: Seat 1 and seat 100 are treated identically by every random choice, and the game is decided the moment one of them is taken.
redHerring: Setting up a recursion over the number of passengers and solving it.
hints: Which seats can the last passenger possibly end up in?
The last passenger gets either seat 1 or seat 100. Nothing else is left.
Whenever a displaced passenger chooses, are seat 1 and seat 100 treated any differently?
solution:
When the last passenger boards, the remaining seat is either seat 1 (the first passenger's) or seat 100: any other seat $k$ would have been taken by passenger $k$.

Every random choice made along the way (by the first passenger or a displaced one) picks uniformly among free seats, so it is equally likely to hit seat 1 or seat 100. The first of these two seats to be taken decides the outcome, and by symmetry each is equally likely to be first. Answer: $\tfrac12$.
